_comment: Sourced from Figma 'Lumen-AI-Design-System' file, page 'Design Tokens' > '02 Typography' (fileKey GJBYRm6ySR7XIECFcHMgy2, node 428:13769). Font family, as last read from that Figma source: Inter (UI text), Roboto Mono (code) — see the 2026-07-27 note at the end of this comment for a direct product decision that has since diverged from it, not yet reconciled back into Figma. H1-H6/Body/Label/Overline/Caption/Code map directly onto this scale's tiers: display-*=H1-H3, headline-*=H4-H6, title-* sits between H6 and Body at medium weight (Figma has no distinct 'title' tier), label-*/body-*/overline/caption/code-* are exact matches. button-* is a separate legacy scale read directly off the earlier Button page. standard-button-* is the current Instrument Sans Medium 12/14/16/18px scale from node 1034:4459, with Figma's normal line height and 1% letter spacing. chat-message/chat-caption/chat-label (added 2026-07-26, chat-label removed then re-added 2026-07-27) are sourced from AIPanel (node 1079:3141) and the separate 'AI Conversation Components' documentation frame (node 1412:3030) via get_design_context's reported text styles: chat-message is the 'Body/Medium' style (Instrument Sans 16/18/400) used for bubble content; chat-caption is the 'Caption/Large' style (Space Mono 14/18/400, 0.2% letter-spacing = 0.028px at this size) used for the timestamp divider and response-metadata text (branch/edited); chat-label is the 'Body/Small' style (Instrument Sans 14/16/400) used for the 'Suggested follow-ups' section label that node 1412:3030's response-actions anatomy has (a section genuinely distinct from the in-bubble follow-ups the canonical 1079:3141 component uses, not a replacement for it — chat-label was briefly removed as apparently-unused before this distinction was made clear). None of the three exactly matches an existing tier at the same pairing, so new purpose-named tokens were added rather than reusing a coincidentally-close one, consistent with this file's existing app-*/ai-library-* convention. 2026-07-27: Inter and Roboto Mono were removed system-wide at direct user request ('remove both fonts'), independent of any Figma change — Figma was unreachable at the time (MCP disconnected), so this was NOT verified against or reconciled back into the Figma source, and the tokens below are now out of sync with the Figma-documented family names above until that reconciliation happens. `sans` and `brand` (previously Inter-only) now use Instrument Sans as their primary face instead, matching `interface`'s existing choice rather than leaving them with no named webfont; `interface` itself no longer lists Inter as a fallback behind Instrument Sans. `mono` (previously Roboto Mono-only) now uses Space Mono; `documentation-mono` (previously Space Mono with a Roboto Mono fallback) simplified to just Space Mono, since its only other named face no longer exists. Neither Space Mono nor Roboto Mono was ever loaded as a webfont via the Storybook Google Fonts import (confirmed: no `@import`/`@font-face` for either anywhere in the repo) — both always relied on the browser's own font matching/system fallback, so this change has no webfont-loading impact for the mono families. Instrument Sans's own Google Fonts import gained weight 700 (previously only 400/500/600) to preserve the brand-mark tokens (`app-logo`/`app-logo-compact`, both weight 700) now that they render in Instrument Sans instead of the Inter import that already covered 600/700.
